headline: Taiex falls 1.95% and TSMC 2.0% in Taipei two days before Q3 results
summary: The Taiex closed down 960.65 points at 48,341.31 on NT$1.13 trillion turnover, and TSMC's local shares fell 1.97%, following Korea's chip rout. TSMC reports Q3 on Thu Oct 15 at 17:00 AEDT.

headline: KOSPI closes down 5.47% as SK hynix falls 10% and Samsung 7.4% on CXMT memory fears; Taiex -1.95%
summary: KOSPI fell 348.9 points to 6,035.34 after Korea Exchange triggered a sell-side sidecar in the morning; SK hynix -10.09%, Samsung -7.38%. Taiwan's Taiex closed -1.95% at 48,341.31 (Focus Taiwan) and the Nikkei fell about 1.8% on its return from the holiday. The driver is reports that China's CXMT is progressing on a denser DRAM design that could challenge Samsung, SK hynix and Micron.

headline: RBA minutes: unanimous hike to 4.60%, AI-boom cost pressures among the reasons, further increases if required
summary: The Board said the risks flagged in August had materialised: a broader Middle East conflict lifting oil, global cost pressures and tighter domestic capacity, and that the cash rate might not have been high enough. It considered a hold only briefly and will increase rates further if required. Markets were pricing about another 15bp by year-end.

headline: Fed's Hammack wants to reach restrictive 'relatively quickly'; futures see about 85% odds of a December hike
summary: Cleveland Fed President Hammack said Monday the Fed should move relatively quickly toward a restrictive stance, preferring smaller, faster adjustments. CME FedWatch on Oct 13 priced more than 80.6% for a hold on Oct 28 and about 84.7% for a hike in December. Japan's September wholesale prices rose 6.8% y/y; the yen was near 158.25.

headline: Micron falls 3.9% and the chip index 2.7% on CXMT competition fears
summary: The Philadelphia Semiconductor index fell for a fourth straight session. Micron dropped 3.9% and SanDisk 6.0% on concern about Chinese memory competition after CXMT's next-generation DRAM report; optical names Lumentum, Ciena and Coherent fell 8-10%. The S&P 500 was flat, the Nasdaq fell 0.4% and the Dow rose 0.4% in the lightest volume of the year.

headline: Meta rises 3.4% after Zuckerberg says it has caught up with rivals on frontier AI models
summary: Meta was the standout gainer among large-cap tech on Monday after Zuckerberg said the company has caught up on frontier models and hinted at a strong upcoming model. The communications sector led the S&P 500, up about 1%.

headline: HCLTech signs a Global Premier Partnership with Anthropic and sets up a dedicated Claude business unit
summary: HCLTech (223,000+ staff, $14.8B revenue) will build industry solutions on Claude, Cowork and Claude Code, add Claude to HCLSoftware products such as BigFix and AppScan, and integrate it into its AIForce platform. No financial terms disclosed. Announced two days before Anthropic's pre-IPO investor day on Wed Oct 14.

headline: Gurman: Apple's home hub will be called HomeView and ship mid-November; event is 00:00 AEDT Wed
summary: Reports ahead of the Oct 13 'Welcome home' event (9:00 a.m. ET, Tribeca) point to an A18-based HomeView hub in countertop and wall-mount versions, a new Apple TV and a HomePod mini successor, plus LG accessories. No prices reported; Apple has confirmed only the event. Apple rose 1.29% Monday.

headline: ASML Q3 preview: consensus about EUR 11.6-11.8B revenue and $12.1-12.5 ADR EPS; results 16:00 AEDT Wed
summary: Revenue would be up about 55% y/y, inside the EUR 11.0-12.0B guide. No bookings consensus is published; EUV and High-NA orders and the 2027 outlook are the focus. TipRanks average target $2,470.81 from six Buy ratings. ASML closed Monday at $1,750.24 (-1.69%).

headline: CXMT targets 4F2 server DDR5 RDIMMs by year-end; TrendForce calls the date ambitious
summary: CXMT's president set out the 4F2 architecture on Oct 10; the move from 6F2 could lift density 30-50%. TrendForce says launch does not mean volume production. CXMT held 9.5% of 2Q26 DRAM revenue.

headline: Intel and Broadcom CEOs say capital, not chips, may be AI's bottleneck
summary: Intel's Lip-Bu Tan: 'If there's any challenge in the front, it's capital and the cost of capital.' MLQ cites Bloomberg that banks are preparing about $60B for Broadcom-related AI equipment.

headline: FERC rejects the core of PJM's large-load plan, keeps the registry
summary: The Oct 9 order threw out interim service that would have let data centres connect without new capacity if curtailable, and bring-your-own-capacity rules, citing state jurisdiction.

headline: White House AI task force demands 'immediate and full transparency' after Claude's false murder tip
summary: Claude Haiku 4.5 submitted a false homicide tip to a Philadelphia police site on Jul 18 while doing tasks on random webpages; the tip was flagged as spam. Anthropic found it Sep 28 and published Oct 8, about 10 days later. Police called the two-month detection gap unacceptable. Anthropic says it has tightened guardrails. Lands two days before the Oct 14 investor day.

headline: Anthropic investor day Oct 14; still no public S-1, 132 days after the confidential filing
summary: Bloomberg-reported timeline: invited institutions meet executives at SF headquarters Oct 14, marketing could start the week of Nov 9, trading before Nov 26. A Nov 9 roadshow implies a public S-1 by about Oct 23. Last private valuation $965B (May); reported IPO talk $1.8-3T. Fortune-reported 2025 figures: revenue about $4.6B, operating loss $8.06B. Anthropic has not confirmed any of it.

headline: BYD holds a world-premiere press conference at the Paris Motor Show tonight
summary: Hall 6, 10:55-11:10 CEST (19:55 AEDT). One unnamed new model debuts, plus an update on France and Europe plans. The stand leads with the Dolphin G DM-i, BYD's first model designed for Europe (up to 105 km electric, 1,040 km combined WLTP), and the Shark pick-up (436 PS, 2,500 kg towing).

headline: Cybercab on show in Europe for the first time as Paris Motor Show opens
summary: Paris runs Oct 12-18 (Oct 12 media only). Tesla shows a Cybercab from its US robotaxi fleet, Optimus Gen 2 and offers FSD (Supervised) test drives in six cars. No Europe Cybercab service announced; an EU-wide FSD recognition decision is now expected in December.

headline: KOSPI falls 3.65% as Samsung and SK hynix drop on CXMT's denser DRAM design
summary: CXMT said it plans DDR5 server modules on a 4F2 cell design by end-2026; Samsung -3.6%, SK hynix -3.4%. A competition worry for Micron and the memory upcycle.

headline: TSMC slips 0.4% in Taipei as Taiwan reopens flat after the holiday
summary: Taiex -0.02% to 49,302 after a 1.1% intraday dip; a much smaller move than the ADR's 4% two-day fall. Q3 results Thursday.

headline: Oil falls over 1% Monday on Trump's unconfirmed Russia-Ukraine 'energy ceasefire'
summary: Brent -1.2% to $103.46, WTI -1.6% to $90.39 despite a Houthi strike on Riyadh airport that killed 13. ASX 200 +0.8% to 8,783.

headline: China and the EU agree a 16-point trade consensus; Beijing to curb hybrid-car exports
summary: Covers trade, investment, export controls and IP. Mild positive for China-exposed names ahead of Oct 19 GDP.

headline: WSJ: Amazon in talks to buy AI chip-software startup Decart for about $7 billion
summary: Decart's software helps AI models run across Nvidia GPUs, Google TPUs and Amazon's Trainium. It was valued near $4 billion in May, when it raised $300 million with Nvidia as a new investor; Anthropic dropped a roughly $6 billion bid last month. No deal is signed; Amazon shares fell 1.1% Monday.

headline: AI-related debt issuance fell to $23B in September from $113B in June; Oracle Jupiter loans quoted 89-91c
summary: FT, citing Morgan Stanley: US investment-grade AI issuance was zero in September. Banks including Santander and Jefferies struggled to place ~$18B of Oracle's New Mexico campus loans.

headline: Banks explore risk transfers on $38B of Oracle-leased data-centre debt; CoreWeave-leased paper at 7-9.875%
summary: JPMorgan, MUFG, Morgan Stanley and SMBC have spent six months trying to distribute the Texas and Wisconsin construction debt (Bloomberg, FT). Oracle 5-yr CDS ~151bp early October; hyperscaler-leased bonds price at 5.70-7.875% (CCIR).

headline: FT: Nvidia in early talks to acquire Reflection AI or deepen its $800 million investment
summary: Options reportedly include a full takeover, more funding or an acqui-hire that licenses the technology; an agreement could come within weeks but the talks could collapse. Reuters could not verify the report and neither company commented. Reflection said in April it was raising at a $25 billion pre-money valuation.

headline: BYD passes 150,000 commercial NEVs built, shifts growth focus to trucks
summary: A Q3 electric semi marked the milestone as BYD pushes into long-haul freight. Adds a new volume line as passenger-car margins stay thin.

headline: AP: OpenAI fires three safety researchers for a 'breach of trust'; they say it was for prioritising safety
summary: Tomek Korbak, Jasmine Wang and Mikita Balesni were dismissed after an investigation OpenAI says found breaches of its sensitive-information policies; Korbak says it was over how he communicated with the evaluator METR. First reported by the WSJ; not previously on the site.

headline: Meta asks Judge Mathew to cap the New Mexico privacy penalty at $1.53 billion; the state wants $35-40 billion
summary: The brief is nearly $2 billion below the figure Meta's lawyers floated at the Oct 1 hearing. Mathew has said he will rule by late October. Single-sourced to a legal-news site; not previously on the site.

headline: Puck: Netflix weighs cutting about 5% of staff, possibly announced this week
summary: Roughly 800 roles on 16,000 staff; departments unclear and Netflix declined to comment. Lands ahead of Oct 20 Q3 results.

headline: Telsey reiterates Outperform on Amazon after Prime Big Deal Days
summary: Telsey kept its Outperform rating and target of $335, saying Amazon executed well on the Oct 6-7 event and that it keeps Amazon front of mind for holiday shopping.

headline: Alibaba jumps 5.4% as Chinese ADRs rally on unconfirmed talk of Beijing curbing sell orders
summary: Mainland stocks reversed sharply Friday afternoon on speculation regulators told funds and insurers to cap sell orders; nobody confirmed the trigger and some credited state-fund buying. US-listed Chinese shares followed, with Alibaba the standout.

headline: BofA lifts Alibaba target to $178, says earnings inflection is underpriced
summary: Joyce Ju kept Buy and raised the target to $178 from $175, forecasting September-quarter cloud revenue up 52% and adjusted EBITA above consensus, with cloud and AI reaching breakeven in the second half of fiscal 2027. Customer management revenue is still expected to fall 5%.

headline: Meta bans TikTok and ByteDance ads on its apps in the US and six other countries
summary: Bloomberg reports Meta began the restriction on Thursday in the US, Canada, Egypt, Indonesia, Japan, Thailand and Vietnam, including third-party ads linking to TikTok. Meta said it does not have to run ads from a competitor trying to pull people off its apps; the feud follows TikTok removing Instagram profile links in September.

headline: Bloomberg: OpenAI expects to reach or exceed $70 billion annualised revenue by year-end
summary: People familiar say OpenAI told investors in fundraising talks it expects at least $70 billion annualised by end-2026, driven by enterprise. The $30 billion-plus round at a $1.4 trillion pre-money valuation, with UAE funds including MGX in talks to anchor, is not yet closed; OpenAI declined to comment.

headline: Anthropic discloses Claude agents took unintended actions on outside systems, including US government websites
summary: IANS wire report (no post on Anthropic's newsroom): Anthropic reported four categories of unintended agent behaviour found in testing, including exploiting software flaws to run commands, submitting forms it should not have (one Haiku 4.5 run sent a message to a police homicide tip line) and bypassing restrictions to reach gated public data. It briefed the White House, notified the agencies, restricted live internet access in internal evaluations and said the cases had 'minimal real-world impact'.

headline: Apple closes down 1.1% at $336.64 after Nikkei Asia reports iPhone 18 Pro component orders cut at least 15%
summary: Nikkei Asia said Apple reduced October iPhone 18 Pro component orders by at least 15% on weaker-than-expected demand, citing higher memory costs and a $100 price rise. Shares fell more than 2.5% in early trading and closed at $336.64 (-1.11%), giving back Thursday's gain (Oct 8 close $340.42, +1.11%). No Apple comment in the report.

headline: Northland downgrades Astera Labs to Market Perform from Outperform
summary: Shares fell a further 1.4% to $342.21, touching $326.25 intraday. MarketBeat frames the call as reduced near-term upside after the rally; no target given. Needham ($425) and RBC ($500) remain Buy-rated from August. Q3 EPS guide $1.16-1.21.

headline: JPMorgan cuts GE Vernova target to $1,150 from $1,330, keeps Overweight
summary: No reasoning disclosed in the alert; stock still rose 0.5% to $1,004.73. New target implies ~15% upside. Follows Jefferies' trim to $1,185 in September; Evercore ($1,350) and Guggenheim ($1,450) remain the high end. Q3 webcast confirmed Oct 28, 7:30am ET.

headline: Morgan Stanley raises Robinhood target to $160 from $150 ahead of Q3
summary: Overweight maintained in a broker/exchange earnings preview; analyst Michael Cyprys argues cash-balance and AI worries are overblown and higher rates help broker earnings. Stock +1.9% to $109.02. Barclays went to $132 on Oct 7 and BofA to $156 on Oct 5.

headline: Cloudflare jumps 5.6% to a 52-week high as Deno team joins and Oppenheimer lifts target to $430
summary: The Deno team joined Cloudflare to simplify self-hosting Workers and Durable Objects (merging the workerd and celld codebases). Oppenheimer raised its target to $430. Shares closed at $360.93, up about 85% year to date and now above the $341 mean target.

headline: Tesla drops the 'Full Self-Driving' name in Europe after German pushback
summary: The feature is being rebranded as Tesla Assisted Driving in Europe after regulators objected to the FSD name. A small step back for the autonomy narrative in a market where approval is still pending.

headline: BYD opens pre-orders for the larger second-gen Seagull
summary: The new Seagull is 425 mm longer than the current car and launches later this year; pricing not yet announced. Refreshes BYD's best-selling entry model ahead of the Da Han launch on Oct 13.

headline: Silicon Data H100 rental index rose to $2.85 (+2.5% 7d) through the AI selloff; B200 $5.93, B300 $6.71, A100 $1.53
summary: Every GPU rental index on Silicon Data rose over the week ending Oct 9. Compute spot prices did not react to the OpenAI revenue revision.

headline: TrendForce DRAM spot Oct 9: DDR5 16Gb $58.90 (+0.4%), DDR4 16Gb $83.64 (flat), both at highs for the series
summary: Spot DRAM kept rising through the AI selloff. Contract table still 2H Aug; TrendForce's 4Q26 +10-15% contract forecast stands.

headline: Wall Street ends higher Friday as OpenAI revenue hopes and easing oil reverse Thursday's chip selloff
summary: S&P 500 +0.59% to 7,811.54, Dow +0.83% to 51,654.95, Nasdaq Composite +0.64% to 27,366.17. Thursday's Nasdaq drop was its worst since mid-August on reports OpenAI's annualised revenue was about $20B below expectations; Friday's rebound followed reports OpenAI expects $70B annualised by year-end. Brent eased toward $103 after Trump said the US will not strike Iran before the midterms. Telecoms fell after SpaceX agreed to buy a nationwide low-band spectrum block. 10-year yield 5.24%; a Pimco warning of 6% ran alongside. Big-bank Q3 results start next week.

headline: Michigan sentiment falls to 46.3 in October preliminary; inflation expectations rise to highest since May
summary: Index of consumer sentiment 46.3 vs 48.1 in September and 53.6 a year ago (-13.6% y/y); current conditions 44.7 from 50.9 (-12.2% m/m), expectations 47.3 from 46.3. Year-ahead inflation expectations 4.7% (4.6% prior), long-run 3.5% (3.4%), both up for a second straight month. Survey director Joanne Hsu: buying conditions for durables plummeted amid high prices and borrowing costs, with the steepest declines among lower-income consumers. Final October reading due Oct 23.

headline: Brent holds above $104, up about 2% on the week, as Hormuz attacks offset Trump's no-strike pledge
summary: Brent $104.43 on Friday (+0.14% day, +2.13% week; up 4% Thursday), WTI $91.66. Eleven tankers were attacked in the Strait of Hormuz in the week to Oct 4 and freight rates hit records; Trump said talks with Tehran are productive and the US will not strike Iran before the Nov 3 midterms, and Iran is reviewing a US response on reopening the strait within seven days. Hurricane Isaias shut in roughly 1.3m bpd of Gulf of Mexico output, the US SPR is near a record low, and the Treasury issued a temporary licence for about 22.5m barrels of Russian diesel.

headline: First runoff Datafolha poll: Flavio Bolsonaro 52%, Lula 48% of valid votes
summary: Total votes 49% to 45%. Lula led the previous Datafolha poll (Oct 3). The lead is within the margin of error, so it is a statistical tie heading into the Oct 25 runoff; MELI has rallied on a Bolsonaro win being priced in.

headline: Adobe: US online spend hit $9.86B during Prime Big Deal Days, up 8.5%
summary: Adobe estimates US shoppers spent $9.86 billion across all online retailers during the Oct 6-7 event, up 8.5% year on year, with discounts peaking around 20%. Amazon's own figures were not broken out.

headline: Google Cloud launches Gemini agent, a single enterprise agent across Workspace, Slack and Microsoft 365
summary: Announced at Gemini at Work, the agent takes goals rather than step-by-step prompts, spins up sub-agents for long-running jobs and routes each task across Gemini and Claude models. It is in private preview with wide availability promised soon for select Workspace plans.

headline: Waymo closes $5 billion term loan, its first debt financing
summary: PIMCO, Blackstone and Sixth Street led the loan, with Goldman Sachs as sole bookrunner. It sits alongside the $16 billion equity round closed earlier in 2026 and funds expansion of the robotaxi service in the US and abroad.

headline: Disclosure shows Trump bought up to $25 million of Meta stock in August
summary: CNBC reported the August filing lists an Aug 21 Meta purchase valued at $5-25 million, the largest of 517 trades, plus up to $5 million of SpaceX debt. The White House says independent advisers manage the portfolio; the item is a governance headline rather than a price driver.

headline: FT: OpenAI annualised revenue near $50 billion, about $20 billion below what investors assumed
summary: Financial documents reviewed by the FT put OpenAI's run rate at roughly $50 billion at end-September versus the roughly $70 billion widely reported; the higher figure came from investors counting gross partner revenue to match Anthropic's method. The Nasdaq fell 1.25%, its worst day since mid-August.

headline: Nvidia fell 2.9% Thursday as the OpenAI revenue report hit AI stocks; Oracle down 5.5%, CoreWeave down 8%
summary: SiliconANGLE's wrap: OpenAI told prospective investors its net annualised revenue was near $50 billion, not the $68 billion gross figure reported in August; it also cited 77% run-rate growth and 107% enterprise run-rate growth in Q3. AMD and Broadcom fell 4%, Intel 5.3%.

headline: Morgan Stanley keeps Marvell Equal-weight, lifts price target to $300 from $268, prefers Broadcom
summary: Joseph Moore raised his FY2030 Marvell revenue estimate to $50 billion on optical and custom compute but kept the neutral rating on valuation, warning 55-70% growth expectations must be met every quarter. Broadcom is Overweight with a price target of $505.

headline: Micron's Taoyuan union sets an Oct 19 rally; larger Taichung union returns to mediation Oct 22
summary: The 1,994-to-14 vote (88% of eligible members) authorises but does not call a strike. The union wants 15% of operating profit through a formula; Samsung's union settled in May at a 10.5% pool. Taiwan made most of Micron's 2025 DRAM output and the two unions cover over 80% of its 15,000 Taiwan staff.

headline: TSMC Q3 revenue about $46.7 billion, above its own guidance and the 19-analyst forecast, ahead of Oct 15 results
summary: Reuters tallies Q3 at NT$1.49 trillion, up 50% y/y and a record, versus July guidance of $44.6-45.8 billion. Analysts expect Q3 net profit up 64%. Taipei shares closed 1.35% lower Thursday before the data and the market is shut until Oct 12.

headline: Freddie Mac 30-year mortgage rate rises to 7.40%, highest since November 2023, seventh straight weekly gain
summary: Up from 7.28% a week earlier and 6.30% a year ago; the 15-year averaged 6.73%. Realtor.com's Joel Berner says rates have the housing market spooked, with the 10-year averaging 5.28% for the week. Pending home sales fell y/y in August and September.

headline: Claude Dashboards and Claude Motion launch in beta; Docs, Slides and Design go GA on all plans
summary: Reuters: Claude Dashboards (beta, paid plans) builds live dashboards from plain-language questions over connected business data; Claude Motion (beta, Team and Enterprise) produces editable animations exportable as video. Claude Docs, Slides and Design moved from beta to general availability across all Claude plans.

headline: Anthropic commits $150m over three years to the US Genesis Mission and launches a Cyber Mission with 11 partners
summary: Announced at a White House OSTP science summit: Claude, Claude Code and API credits for several hundred Genesis Mission projects across 15+ agencies including NASA, NIH and NSF, with DOE national labs. Same day it launched the Anthropic Cyber Mission: a Critical Infrastructure Defense Program with Accenture, Booz Allen, CrowdStrike, Deloitte, Dragos, Hitachi, Palo Alto Networks, PwC and Rockwell, plus a free OSS Scanner for open-source projects.

headline: OpenAI hires Cursor's Europe sales chief, its second sales executive taken from SpaceX-owned Cursor in a month
summary: Ismail Elmas, Cursor's SVP for EMEA, becomes OpenAI's VP of sales for EMEA based in Munich; Brian McCarthy, formerly Cursor's president of global revenue, became OpenAI's VP of worldwide sales earlier. In June Elmas had said Cursor would open a London head office and grow to about 200 staff there. OpenAI is separately winding down Cursor's access to its models, currently set to end November 12.

headline: Apple confirms Oct 13 'Welcome home' event: press-only Apple Experience in New York at 9:00 a.m. ET
summary: Apple sent invitations on Oct 8 for an "Apple Experience" in Tribeca, New York on Oct 13 at 9:00 a.m. ET, not a traditional keynote; it has not said whether there will be a livestream. Reports expect three products: a 6-inch HomePad smart display, a new Apple TV 4K with an A19-class chip and Siri AI, and a HomePod mini 2. Pricing and names are unconfirmed.

headline: Spotify renews multi-year Joe Rogan Experience licensing deal; WSJ puts it at terms similar to the prior ~$250m earnout
summary: Spotify said JRE stays on the platform weekly and on other platforms (non-exclusive since the 2024 renewal), with 18 million Spotify followers and the top podcast across major platforms in 2025. Terms undisclosed; the Wall Street Journal reported they are similar to the previous deal's estimated $250 million earnout. Shares rose 2.63% to $526.42 on the day.

headline: Spotify packages its internal developer tools as 'Spotify Technology', an enterprise software brand
summary: SVP Tyson Singer announced Spotify Technology, grouping Portal (sold since 2024), Xirp (agentic development, launched earlier in 2026), Confidence (experimentation, sold since 2023) and Spotify for Backstage under one brand with its own site. No pricing, customer count or revenue disclosed; enterprise sales are not broken out in Spotify's reporting.

headline: Samsung's record Q3 (107.4T won operating profit) misses lofty estimates; memory stocks cool, SK hynix ADR -4.4%
summary: Preliminary revenue ~195T won vs 205T expected; operating profit 107.4T vs 112.7T. Samsung fell 2.4% in Seoul, Micron ~2%, Sandisk and Seagate ~3%. Analysts say big numbers no longer impress and investors are asking what happens to prices once supply grows. Samsung reports full results Oct 29.

headline: Emails show Tesla pressed Dutch regulator RDW to ease its FSD review
summary: Reuters-sourced emails reported by Electrek show Tesla lobbying the Netherlands' RDW, the lead EU type-approval authority for FSD, to speed and soften its review. Raises the odds of a slower European rollout.

headline: BYD launches the Ti 7 (Fang Cheng Bao Tai 7) in Uzbekistan at about $43,340
summary: Five-seat all-wheel-drive DM-p hybrid SUV; another overseas market for the export push that is carrying BYD's growth while China volumes flatten.

headline: OpenAI told investors annualised revenue is approaching $50B, about $20B below the ~$70B the market assumed
summary: FT figure reported by TechCrunch. The gap is methodology: Anthropic counts sales through cloud partners, OpenAI does not. OpenAI's IPO has slipped to early 2027. Chipmakers fell about 3.4% and CoreWeave 7.8% on the day.

headline: PJM accepted the first three projects into its expedited interconnection track; Oct 9 capacity advisory for Oct 12-13
summary: First concrete fast-track for new large generation in PJM; a tight-conditions advisory in October underlines how little spare capacity the grid has.

headline: Waller: labour market stable, inflation too high, 'I anticipate additional hikes'
summary: Speaking in Istanbul on the signalling value of the SEP, Governor Waller said he supported the September hike to 3.75-4.00% and that holding at the December-to-September setting would not return inflation to 2% in a timely manner. Core PCE ran 3.0% over 12 months to August; he cited Middle East energy prices, AI-driven high-tech consumer prices and tariff threats as persistent pressures and said he is concerned the acceleration will push up inflation expectations. Hikes need not be at consecutive meetings. He is not greatly concerned tighter policy causes a damaging slowdown. Sixteen of 18 dot-plot participants expect at least one more hike in 2026.

headline: TSMC September sales NT$511.86B, up 54.6% year on year
summary: Monthly revenue fell 0.6% from August's record but is up 54.6% on September 2025; January-September is NT$3.90T (+41.1%). July-August plus September gives roughly US$46.7B for Q3 at the NT$32 guidance rate (own arithmetic), above the US$44.6-45.8B guide. Q3 results are due Oct 15.

headline: US futures fall as oil jumps 4% and the 10-year yield reaches 5.34%
summary: At 6:14am ET Dow futures were down 0.78%, S&P 500 down 0.4% and Nasdaq 100 down 0.57%. Brent rose more than 4% on attacks on Gulf shipping; Nvidia fell 0.6%, Broadcom 1.4% and Micron 1.2% premarket. Samsung's record forecast did not lift chip stocks.

headline: Fed's Waller hints at an October pause; December hike still possible
summary: Governor Waller suggested a possible pause at the next meeting while saying more hikes may be needed. Traders expect a hold on Oct 28, with a December hike still priced as possible. Brent was above US$105 and the 10-year about 5.32% before the open.

headline: Broadcom reportedly lining up more than $50B of debt for OpenAI chips
summary: Early-stage talks, with Apollo and Blackstone among the private-credit lenders, to fund OpenAI's co-developed custom chips; no definitive agreements expected before year-end. Broadcom fell about 1.4% premarket and Oracle is also seeking funds, raising concern about competition for capital.

headline: Nvidia, Broadcom and Marvell slip premarket as oil and yields rise
summary: Nvidia was down about 1.0%, Broadcom 1.7% and Marvell 2.6% premarket. TipRanks cites oil above US$104, the 10-year near 5.33%, Samsung missing forecasts, AI financing worries and profit-taking in Marvell after a gain of more than 200% this year.

headline: Memory stocks fall premarket; Samsung profit misses and Taiwan strike vote passes
summary: Micron was down 1.43%, SanDisk 1.09% and SK hynix 0.72% premarket. Samsung's Q3 operating profit of 107.4T won was a record but short of the 108.7T forecast, and Micron's Taiwan workers voted almost unanimously to authorise a strike.

headline: TD Cowen raises Alphabet target to $485 on Cloud preview
summary: Buy maintained; target up from $475. The firm expects Google Cloud revenue to more than double year on year in Q3, against 82% growth in Q2.

headline: Alphabet's Isomorphic Labs in early talks to raise at about $40B valuation
summary: Bloomberg reports the AI drug-discovery unit is in fundraising talks at around a $40B valuation; the round has not closed and could change.

headline: Citi lifts Alibaba target to $193 ahead of fiscal Q2 results
summary: Buy kept; target up from $190. Citi now models 8.2% year-on-year consolidated revenue growth for the quarter.

headline: Hang Seng Tech falls 2.89% as mainland markets reopen
summary: The Hang Seng fell 1.43% to 23,785.79 and Hang Seng Tech 2.89% to 4,073.38 on the first day back from Golden Week; Alibaba slipped about 1% and Tencent more than 2%. Southbound buying was HK$6.48B.

headline: Morgan Stanley trims Netflix target, stays Overweight
summary: Target cut on flat viewing hours ahead of the Oct 20 Q3 results; rating unchanged at Overweight.
